text:
UN General Assembly resolutions are not a formal source of international law under Article 38(1) of the ICJ Statute, because they are generally non-binding recommendations. They can still matter indirectly. They can serve as evidence of customary law (opinio juris), as in the ICJ's *Nicaragua* and *Nuclear Weapons* opinions. They can also help interpret treaties or crystallise emerging norms, and a few bind, such as internal budgetary and organisational decisions or resolutions that restate existing binding law (e.g. the Friendly Relations Declaration).
